summary: The root رصص (rSS) primarily means to make something compact, firm, or closely joined together. It implies a solid, well-arranged structure, like bricks or stones fitted tightly, leaving no gaps.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: رَصَّهُ, (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. رَصُصَ, inf. n. رَصٌّ, (S, M, Msb,) He stuck it (a thing, S, Mgh) together, one part to another, (S, A, Mgh, K,) so that there might be no interstice in it; (Mgh;) joined it together; (Msb, K;) namely, a building; (Msb;) and, (S, * Mgh, K,) inf. n.

رَصَّصَ see 1, in two places. رَصَّصَتْ, (AZ, M,) inf. n. تَرْصِيصٌ, (AZ, S,) She (a woman) put on, or wore, her نِقَاب [a kind of face-veil ] in such a manner that nothing was seen but her eyes: (AZ, S, M:) as also وَصَّصَتْ, (AZ, TA,) or وَصْوَصَتْ: (M:) وصّصت is of the dial. of Temeem. (AZ, TA.) رصّص (tropical:) He was importunate, or urgent, in asking, or begging. (Fr, TA.)

تراصّوا They placed themselves close together, (Ks, S, M, A, K,) in a rank, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) in prayer, (A, TA,) and in battle, (TA,) so that there was no intervening space among them; (Ks;) as also: (A:) they placed themselves in a rank, or in ranks, in battle, and in prayer. (M.)
ارتصّت الجَنَادلُ The stones were stuck, or set close, together; as also. (A.) See also 6.
R. Q. 1 رَصْرَصَهُ: see 1, in two places. رَصْرَصَ فِى المَكَانِ He continued, or became fixed or settled, in the place. (IAar, K.)
رَصَصٌ in the teeth is like لَصَصٌ; (M, TA;) and in the teeth signifies [the same, i. e.,] Nearness together. (A, TA. *) See also the next paragraph.

رَصَاصٌ (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and, (M,) or the latter is vulgar, (S,) and not allowable, (K,) or, accord. to AHát, it is correct, and it is quoted by Ez-Zarkashee, and by certain of the Expositors of the Fs, and is the only form mentioned by AHei, (TA,) and, accord. to some of the moderns, also, (MF,) and, (M, TA,) which is a contraction of the first, (TA,) [ Lead; ] a certain mineral, (M,) well known; (S, K;) i. q.
رُصَاصٌ: see the next preceding paragraph.
رِصَاصٌ: see the next preceding paragraph.
رَصِيصٌ: see مَرْصُوصٌ, in two places. A woman's [face-veil of the kind called] نِقَاب drawn near to her eyes. (AA, K.) See also رَصَصٌ.

رَصَاصَةٌ: see رَصَاصٌ. Also, (accord. to a copy of the M,) or, with teshdeed, (K,) Stones cleaving to the circuit of a running spring; and so: (Lth, M, K:) or رصاصة [in my copy of the A written ] signifies a stone: and the pl. is رَصَائِصُ [which is reg. as pl. of either of the above-mentioned forms without tesh-deed but not as pl. of that with teshdeed]. (A.) You say, عَلَى القَبْرِ الرَّصَائِصُ The stones were heaped together upon the grave. (A.) Hence,, (as in the A,) or, (accord.
رُصَاصَةٌ: see رَصَاصَةٌ, in two places.
رَصَّاصٌ [app., accord. to the TA, A manufacturer of lead: or] a seller of lead. (Meyd, in Golius.)
رَصَّاصَةٌ: see رَصَاصَةٌ, in two places.
رَصْرَاصَةٌ: see رَصَاصَةٌ. Hard ground or land. (K.) This is its meaning accord. to IDrd. (TA.)

أَرَصُّ A man whose teeth are near together: (M, A, K:) fem. رَصَّآءُ. (M, A.) And the fem., applied to a woman, Impervia coëunti; as also. (M.) رَصَّآءُ الفَخِ ِيْنِ A woman whose thighs are close together. (A.) فَخِ ٌ رَصَّآءُ A thigh that cleaves, or sticks, to its fellow. (O, K.)
أُرْصُوصَةٌ A [ cap of the kind called ] قَلَنْسُوَة like a melon. (O, K.)
مُرَصَّصٌ: see what follows, in two places.

مَرْصُوصٌ A building having its several parts stuck together, (S, A, Mgh, TA,) so that there is no interstice in it: (Mgh:) or a building made firm and compact: (M:) and signifies the same; (A, Mgh, TA;) and so. (M, TA.) You say also, بَيْضٌ Eggs [ set ] one upon another. (K.) A thing done over, or overlaid, ( مَطْلِىٌّ,) with رَصَاص; as also. (S, K.) بِئْرٌ مَرْصُوصَةٌ A well cased with رَصَاص. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
